column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If people were given according to their claims, men would claim the wealth and the blood of others.
But the burden of proof is on the claimant, and the oath is on the one who denies.” A hadith reported by al-Bayhaqī and others in this way; part of it is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs.
Bi-daʿwāhum (“according to their claims”): merely on their claiming that they have a right.
Al-muddaʿī (“the claimant”): the one who has the right [due to him]. And the defendant (al-muddaʿā ʿalayh):
the one who owes the right.
No one is to be judged in favour of merely on his claim and his wish.
It is not permissible to judge except by what has come in the Sharīʿah, even if the claimant's truthfulness seems most likely.
The oath is on the defendant if he denies, and the burden of proof is on the claimant.

This hadith takes into account the general welfare of people: protecting their lives and wealth, setting their society right, preventing its discord, and establishing security in the land and among the people.
The noble Prophet ﷺ tells us that if every person were given whatever he claimed and wished, some people would go so far as to claim that so-and-so's wealth was theirs,
and another would claim that so-and-so had deliberately killed his son, so that he could be executed in retaliation; order would break down and the strong would overpower the weak,

and chaos and strife would prevail. But it is part of the wisdom of the Sharīʿah that it placed the burden of proof on the one who claims a right, because he claims what is contrary to the apparent state of affairs,
and the oath on the one who denies, because the default is freedom from liability, so that security is established and rights and lives are protected.
The poet said about establishing the truth:
I saw you, O best of all creation, / spread forth a Book that came with the truth as a guide.
You set straight the path of truth after it had become crooked, / when long ago its pillar had collapsed.
